title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measures the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for intent→configuration artifacts produced by a declared LLM (requested: gpt-5-mini). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. Deterministic_netops_validator_v5 detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call); stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1. These artifact-grounded outcomes fall far below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, run-accounting diagnostics, artifact-grounded interpretation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and reproducibility guidance pointing to the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational safety requires that generated artifacts satisfy syntactic, semantic and workflow constraints; the common mitigation pattern is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, often augmented by sandboxed emulation that can reveal runtime-only failures. Prior surveys and system reports document architectures that pair LLM generation with validators, verifiers, and emulators but provide little large-scale paired measurement of the marginal value added by guarded runtime stages [1], [2], [3].

Research question and contributions. We preregistered a paired confirmatory design to answer: For synthetic intent→configuration tasks and under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Our contributions are: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful execution (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e); (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with exact numeric reporting; (3) concrete run-accounting diagnostics linking the unique discordant outcome to guarded-stage activity; and (4) an artifact-grounded interpretation explaining the near-zero marginal effect and identifying regimes where guarded stages are likely to add substantive value.
sections.related_work:
Workflow-centric mitigation and generate→validate patterns. Surveys and system papers document architectures that pair LLM generation with validators, verifiers, and sandboxed execution to improve correctness of generated artifacts in NetOps and adjacent domains; these works call for workflow-centred evaluation but stop short of large-scale paired estimates of guarded-stage marginal benefits [1], [2].

Verifier-assisted generation and empirical evidence. Transfer of program- and specification-verification techniques into generation tasks shows external verifiers and emulators often catch errors language models miss; empirical studies in code/specification generation and NetOps prototypes report improved correctness with external checking but heterogeneous gains depending on task and evaluator coverage [3], [4]. These findings motivated our preregistered paired design: instead of ranking models, we measure the guarded-stage marginal detection effect under tightly controlled conditions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design freeze. We froze a machine-readable preregistration before any confirmatory observations. Design: paired-binary with shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial candidate per task reused by both baseline and guarded conditions). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples; preregistered minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20.

Task bank, vendors, and inclusion rules. Confirmatory items were synthetic intent→configuration tasks from intent_configuration_repair_v1. The bank covered three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf-spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance; parser failures triggered the preregistered deterministic missingness policy (up to two automatic reseeds; irrecoverable failures would be excluded and replaced). In the confirmatory run there were zero irrecoverable parser exclusions (analysis/missingness_summary.csv) and complete_pair_count = 720.

Model sampling semantics and shared_initial_candidate. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses). The archived execution/model_configuration.json records max_output_tokens = 2000 and temperature = null. We emphasize: temperature = null indicates the client request omitted an explicit temperature parameter; null does not imply temperature=0 or provider-side determinism. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced: a single sampled initial candidate per pair (shared) was recorded and reused by both baseline and guarded analyses; therefore any between-condition discordance must arise solely from (i) guarded-stage emulation observations not encoded as validator violations or (ii) a permitted downstream repair-stage invocation recorded in run accounting. This design choice isolates guarded-stage contributions and removes between-condition generation variability.

Baseline validator and guarded pipeline. Baseline: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performing full intent-constraint validation (syntax, command ordering/workflow, required-field presence, and policy-level constraints) and producing a binary detected/not-detected outcome per episode under the scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation. Guarded: baseline validator followed by an automated sandboxed emulation harness that executes the candidate in an emulated instance of the declared topology and reports runtime observations beyond static checks. Repair policy: at most one repair-stage model invocation per task (preregistered). Execution adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1.

Sampling plan, power and analysis executor. Confirmatory Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440). Primary analysis: paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor (exact McNemar two-sided plus paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI via 10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness handling: complete_pair_primary (exclude irrecoverable technical pairs) with a preregistered sensitivity analysis treating irrecoverable failures as nondetections; none were needed because there were zero technical exclusions.

Execution accounting and provenance checks. Execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) records model_calls_used = 721, completed_episode_count = 1440, failed_episode_count = 0. Deterministic reconciliation artifacts and provider_call_audit report stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1. Contamination and provenance checks (artifact hashing and validator/config checks) were performed per the preregistration; the confirmatory set produced no contamination flags (analysis/contamination_summary.csv). All per-episode validator_trace and emulation observations were archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ for reproducibility.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (complete paired set Npairs = 720). Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv) report: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (detected by guarded only), n01 = 0 (detected by baseline only), n00 = 0 (detected by neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All numerical values are reproduced verbatim from analysis/results.json and analysis artifacts.

Run accounting and discordant-pair attribution. The execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json confirm model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call) with provider_call_audit stage_counts showing a single repair invocation. The single n10 discordance therefore corresponds to guarded-stage activity recorded in the archived artifacts. For reproducible verification we give an explicit artifact pointer: locate the unique record in execution/raw_results.jsonl (archived SHA-256 = df367ecc40a6f0eaf402129260e11d8450884a4ea5fdb94a602e0d2513aef0e8) whose fields baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1; that record's pair_id field (archived in the same JSONL record) identifies the discordant pair and contains the validator_trace and repair_provider_trace fields that link the guarded detection to the single documented repair-stage call. Independent auditors can reproduce this mapping by (a) opening execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256 above), (b) locating the unique record where baseline_score == 0 and guarded_score == 1, and (c) following that record's pair_id and validator_trace/repair_provider_trace entries; provider_call counts are corroborated via analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json's provider_call_audit.

Representative per-episode diagnostics. Representative archived examples (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json) include detailed validator_trace objects showing normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, validation_before/after, validator_version = 5.0, and violation_count. These traces illustrate that the vast majority of shared_initial candidates complied with validator rules (violation_count = 0) and that sandboxed emulation observations largely duplicated validator findings. The representative artifacts document the validator ceiling effect evident in the aggregate counts.

Missingness, exclusions, and preregistration compliance. The preregistered missingness policy was applied deterministically; analysis/missingness_summary.csv documents complete_pairs = 720 and zero failed episodes. There were no deviations from the preregistration affecting the primary estimand. The contamination summary is empty for the confirmatory set (analysis/contamination_summary.csv).
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded explanation for the negligible guarded benefit. The archived evidence supports three concrete factors.

1) Validator ceiling effect. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 provided near-universal coverage for the curated syntactic and explicit semantic properties encoded in the synthetic task bank; baseline success rate = 0.9986111111111111. The validator's rule set covered the workflow patterns used in task generation (shutdown-configure-restore, make-before-break switchover, paired MTU changes), producing a ceiling that leaves little headroom for emulation to add marginal detections.

2) Task curation and inclusion policy. Confirmatory tasks were parser-validated synthetic items designed to exercise workflow policies but not crafted adversarially to evade the validator. That curation concentrates cases inside the validator's coverage envelope and reduces the prevalence of subtle runtime-only failure modes that emulation might reveal.

3) Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. The shared-initial design isolates guarded-stage contributions but suppresses between-condition generation variability; provider_call_audit and deterministic_reconciliation.json record a single repair-stage invocation aligning with the single n10 discordant count. Thus the observed discordance is fully attributable to downstream guarded-stage activity recorded in run accounting rather than generation variability.

Operational implications and boundary conditions. When a high-coverage static validator exists and inputs match its expected patterns (parser-validated, constrained intents), guarded sandboxed emulation may add negligible marginal detection value at aggregate scale. This conditional conclusion must not be generalized: in operational regimes with noisy natural-language intents, adversarial inputs, stateful multi-step interactions, or validator gaps (different vendor behaviors), guarded runtime checks and higher-fidelity emulation remain likely to provide substantive added value. The archived per-episode traces support targeted follow-up hypotheses: (a) adversarial task injection will increase n10 and broaden the CI; (b) combining multiple validator families with complementary rule sets can reduce the ceiling effect.

Statistical sensitivity and interpretation. The study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed discordant counts (n10 = 1) yield an upper 95% CI bound ≈0.00417, demonstrating the realized aggregated effect is orders of magnitude below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest. Interpreting this as a null/near-zero aggregate finding is appropriate for the specific experimental regime (synthetic parser-validated tasks, deterministic validator, shared_initial semantics) but does not imply absence of practical benefit in other regimes.

Threats to validity and limitations (summary). Internal validity: prompt sensitivity and provider-side sampling nondeterminism remain residual uncertainties despite provenance logging; temperature was recorded as null and thus non-determinism cannot be excluded. Construct validity: the binary detected/not-detected scoring rule reflects the preregistered operational safety definition but abstracts away graded risk and rollback-aware impact measures. External validity: single declared/requested model (gpt-5-mini) and single validator family limit generalization across models and validators. Conclusion validity: the study was powered for a large effect (0.20); the observed effect is far smaller and precisely estimated in this regime, but the design cannot exclude non-aggregate per-class or per-vendor pockets of meaningful guarded benefit. See the archived limitations list for full details.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows a single repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, archived per-episode traces permit independent verification of that mapping by inspecting execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256 df367ecc40a6f0eaf402129260e11d8450884a4ea5fdb94a602e0d2513aef0e8) for the unique record where baseline_score == 0 and guarded_score == 1. We interpret the result as arising from validator ceiling effects and curated task design and recommend follow-up work on adversarial and multi-vendor task banks, complementary validator families, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages provide substantive added value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator provide limited ecological diversity and create a ceiling effect for a strong validator; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and provider_call_audit artifacts.
